steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 74.32 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk. It is longer than a 72 in stick: splice two, or cut it from a longer log.

steps.title: Rip it flush
steps.text: This piece stands taller than the frame. Rip 1.43 in off the bark side, parallel to the stick's length, so it sits flush with both faces of the panel. Lay it on a sawn face on the bandsaw or table saw; tilt the blade 22.50° (half the slice's angle) so the cut runs square to the slice's centre line.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 21.1° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 11.2° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 1.18 in along the point, down to 0.96 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 2 (first end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the raw end: 3.06 in along the point; 0.50 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 5.63 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on its mirror on the centre line: it leans 0.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Cut 3 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 0° (blade upright). Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets its mirror on the centre line.

steps.title: Cut 4 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 9.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 68.98 in along the point; 73.57 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 66.03 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the ripped face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a square-ended block 0.34 in long. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 5 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 0.00 in along the point; 0.00 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 0.00 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on its mirror on the centre line: it leans 0.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 73.57 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 68.98 in along the point, 66.03 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as left run 1: standing on its point, bark toward the open side.

steps.title: Rip it flush
steps.text: This piece stands taller than the frame. Rip 1.43 in off the bark side, parallel to the stick's length, so it sits flush with both faces of the panel. Lay it on a sawn face on the bandsaw or table saw; tilt the blade 22.50° (half the slice's angle) so the cut runs square to the slice's centre line.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 30.0° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 9.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 2 (first end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the raw end: 3.54 in along the point; 0.50 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 6.59 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on its mirror on the centre line: it leans 0.0° from the panel's plane.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Rip flush: the standing pieces are taller than the frame; rip 1.43 in off the bark so they sit flush with both faces.
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
20 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 9.0° -- the panel's long edge; bevel half the 18.0° seam fold
20 ends: mitre 60.0°, bevel 0.0° -- meets its mirror on the centre line
fitting: Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
